sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Even if you've never been to L.A.'s Chinatown, you've probably seen it.
sentences.zh: 即使你从未去过洛杉矶的唐人街，你也可能见过它。

sentences.en: Although it doesn't get as much attention as New York or San Francisco's Chinatown,
sentences.zh: 虽然它不像纽约或旧金山的唐人街那样引人注目，

sentences.en: it is a regular shooting location for TV and film.
sentences.zh: 但它却是电视和电影的常驻取景地。

sentences.en: So you may recognize it from movies like Rush Hour or Freaky Friday or, you know, Chinatown.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能在《尖峰时刻》或《辣妈辣妹》或者，你知道的，《唐人街》这样的电影里认出它来。

sentences.en: The most recognizable feature of L.A.'s Chinatown is its central plaza.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶唐人街最显著的特征是它的中央广场。

sentences.en: It's an outdoor pedestrian mall that's almost overwhelmingly colorful.
sentences.zh: 那是一个几乎色彩斑斓到让人应接不暇的户外步行街区。

sentences.en: Producer Vivian Lai.
sentences.zh: 制作人薇薇安·莱。

sentences.en: Brightly painted buildings are topped with sweeping pagoda-style roofs
sentences.zh: 色彩鲜艳的建筑顶部装饰着弧形的宝塔式屋顶，

sentences.en: and then accented with fluorescent neon lacing.
sentences.zh: 并点缀着荧光霓虹灯带。

sentences.en: For decades, Chinatown's central plaza was a thriving tourist area.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，唐人街的中央广场曾是一个繁荣的旅游区。

sentences.en: But by the late 1970s, it had fallen on hard times.
sentences.zh: 但到了70年代末，它陷入了困境。

sentences.en: The neighborhood's neon lights still glowed over the shops and restaurants,
sentences.zh: 街区的霓虹灯依然在商店和餐馆上方闪烁，

sentences.en: but there was no one there to take it all in.
sentences.zh: 但却没有人去欣赏这一切。

sentences.en: And if things had taken a significant nosedive,
sentences.zh: 如果情况进一步恶化，

sentences.en: there really wasn't anyone on the street or going anywhere.
sentences.zh: 街上真的就没人了，也没人会去任何地方。

sentences.en: And, you know, downtown was dead.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，市中心当时死气沉沉的。

sentences.en: It was this deserted Chinatown in 1978 that captured the interest of Paul Greenstein.
sentences.zh: 正是1978年这个荒凉的唐人街引起了保罗·格林斯坦的兴趣。

sentences.en: Back then, Paul was a 20-something.
sentences.zh: 那时，保罗才二十出头。

sentences.en: He liked music and hoped to run his own club as a promoter.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢音乐，希望以推广人的身份经营自己的俱乐部。

sentences.en: Instead, he did a lot of odd jobs around the city for money.
sentences.zh: 但他当时为了钱在城里做了很多零工。

sentences.en: You know, restoring jukeboxes, fixing toys, designing ads for a local cafe.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，修复自动点唱机、修理玩具、为当地咖啡馆设计广告。

sentences.en: Paul would sometimes spend nights wandering around Los Angeles with a friend.
sentences.zh: 保罗有时会和朋友在洛杉矶漫无目的地闲逛。

sentences.en: And one night, he found himself in Central Plaza.
sentences.zh: 一天晚上，他来到了中央广场。

sentences.en: The streets of Chinatown were quiet as always, but a sound caught his attention.
sentences.zh: 唐人街的街道一如既往地安静，但一个声音引起了他的注意。

sentences.en: We can hear this really wild party going on.
sentences.zh: 我们能听到一场非常狂野的派对正在进行。

sentences.en: So we kind of gravitated to where all the noise is coming from.
sentences.zh: 所以我们被吸引到了声音传来的地方。

sentences.en: And there's this place called Madam Wong's.
sentences.zh: 那里有一家叫“黄夫人”的店。

sentences.en: Madam Wong's was a restaurant right in Central Plaza.
sentences.zh: “黄夫人”是位于中央广场的一家餐馆。

sentences.en: If you enter through the famous East Gate, you'll see an ornate two-story building with
sentences.zh: 如果你从著名的东门进入，你会看到一座华丽的两层建筑，

sentences.en: a curved pagoda-style roof and an intricately detailed wooden balustrade lining the balcony.
sentences.zh: 有着弯曲的宝塔式屋顶，阳台上装饰着精致的木制栏杆。

sentences.en: They were obviously, you know, it was packed.
sentences.zh: 显然，你知道，当时里面挤满了人。

sentences.en: And we're looking around, well, there's nobody here in Chinatown, but this place is packed.
sentences.zh: 我们环顾四周，心想，唐人街明明没人，但这地方却挤满了人。

sentences.en: So we go upstairs.
sentences.zh: 于是我们上了楼。

sentences.en: Paul and his friend went up to the second-story entrance of Madam Wong's,
sentences.zh: 保罗和他的朋友走到“黄夫人”的二楼入口，

sentences.en: expecting to have to squeeze his way through the door, but...
sentences.zh: 本以为得挤着进去，但是……

sentences.en: There's nobody there.
sentences.zh: 里面一个人也没有。

sentences.en: It was a recording.
sentences.zh: 那是一段录音。

sentences.en: It was a recording of a party.
sentences.zh: 那是一段派对的录音。

sentences.en: According to Paul, the owners of the restaurant had been blasting party ambiance through speakers
sentences.zh: 据保罗说，餐馆老板一直在通过扬声器播放派对氛围音，

sentences.en: to give off the illusion that it was packed with customers.
sentences.zh: 以此营造出店里顾客盈门的假象。

sentences.en: So we went, oh God, that's so funny.
sentences.zh: 所以我们当时就想，天哪，这太搞笑了。

sentences.en: What a rip.
sentences.zh: 真是个骗局。

sentences.en: This is great.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: We love it.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢这个。

sentences.en: You know, because it was obviously a really lame trick.
sentences.zh: 你知道，因为这显然是个非常拙劣的把戏。

sentences.en: And we thought that was funny.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得这很有趣。

sentences.en: Funny enough that Paul kept coming back to Madam Wong's.
sentences.zh: 有趣到保罗后来一直回到“黄夫人”。

sentences.en: He would ride his motorcycle over to Central Plaza to get lunch regularly
sentences.zh: 他会经常骑着摩托车去中央广场吃午饭，

sentences.en: and would find himself having long conversations with one of the owners of the restaurant,
sentences.zh: 并发现自己经常与餐馆的一位老板进行长谈，

sentences.en: a man named George Wong.
sentences.zh: 那个人叫乔治·黄。

sentences.en: And I'd talk to George and he'd tell me stories, whether they were real or not.
sentences.zh: 我会和乔治聊天，他会给我讲故事，不管是不是真的。

sentences.en: I never know.
sentences.zh: 我从来不知道。

sentences.en: But he'd say, oh God, you know, I was with the Flying Tigers in China
sentences.zh: 但他会说，天哪，你知道，我曾在中国加入过飞虎队，

sentences.en: and I grew up in San Francisco and I had a 1937 Indian just like yours.
sentences.zh: 我在旧金山长大，我有一辆和你一模一样的1937年产印第安摩托车。

sentences.en: And I used to ride it up and down the hills.
sentences.zh: 我过去常骑着它在山上上下穿梭。

sentences.en: And he'd just tell me stories and I'd tell him stories and I'd have a beer and, you know,
sentences.zh: 他会给我讲故事，我也会给他讲故事，我会喝杯啤酒，你知道的，

sentences.en: and then I'd go back to work.
sentences.zh: 然后我就回去工作了。

sentences.en: Madam Wong's was an island-themed restaurant and club.
sentences.zh: “黄夫人”是一家以海岛为主题的餐馆和俱乐部。

sentences.en: They served tropical drinks.
sentences.zh: 他们供应热带饮品。

sentences.en: And at night, Polynesian bands and dancers performed on a tiki-themed stage
sentences.zh: 晚上，波利尼西亚乐队和舞者会在一个提基主题的舞台上表演，

sentences.en: decorated with seashells and dried grass.
sentences.zh: 舞台装饰着贝壳和干草。

sentences.en: Like a lot of businesses in Chinatown, the restaurant wasn't doing well.
sentences.zh: 像唐人街的许多企业一样，这家餐馆经营状况不佳。

sentences.en: By 1978, the tiki craze that gripped the nation had officially burned out.
sentences.zh: 到1978年，席卷全国的提基热潮已经正式消退了。

sentences.en: And Madam Wong's would be lucky to get in a few dozen people during the evenings.
sentences.zh: “黄夫人”晚上能有几十位客人就算走运了。

sentences.en: But Paul had an idea.
sentences.zh: 但保罗有个主意。

sentences.en: One that he hoped would put asses in the seats and Paul on the map.
sentences.zh: 他希望这个主意能让餐馆座无虚席，也能让自己声名鹊起。

sentences.en: Why don't I start a club in this restaurant that's dead all the time?
sentences.zh: 为什么我不在这家一直冷清的餐馆里开个俱乐部呢？

sentences.en: Paul wanted to turn Madam Wong's into a hot new music venue.
sentences.zh: 保罗想把“黄夫人”变成一个热门的新音乐场所。

sentences.en: A venue he would book and promote.
sentences.zh: 一个由他负责预订和推广的场所。

sentences.en: He had all sorts of ideas for the club.
sentences.zh: 他对俱乐部有很多想法。

sentences.en: He imagined putting on rockabilly shows one night,
sentences.zh: 他想象着一晚举办摇滚乐表演，

sentences.en: then the next night a jazz band, even sitar music.
sentences.zh: 下一晚是爵士乐队，甚至还有西塔琴音乐。

sentences.en: So he asked George if he'd be willing to let him book some local musicians at Madam Wong's.
sentences.zh: 于是他问乔治是否愿意让他预订一些当地音乐人在“黄夫人”演出。

sentences.en: Basically, he said, let me talk to my wife.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他说，让我跟我太太商量一下。

sentences.en: So next time I came in, I said, talk to your wife?
sentences.zh: 所以下次我来的时候，我说，跟你太太商量了吗？

sentences.en: And he goes, yeah, she says no.
sentences.zh: 他说，是的，她说不行。

sentences.en: I went, why?
sentences.zh: 我问，为什么？

sentences.en: And he goes, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 他说，我不知道。

sentences.en: She just says no.
sentences.zh: 她就是说不行。

sentences.en: The eponymous Madam Wong, George's wife Esther, passed away in 2005.
sentences.zh: 以其命名的黄夫人，乔治的妻子埃丝特，于2005年去世。

sentences.en: But from every account that I've read or heard, she was a force to be reckoned with.
sentences.zh: 但据我所读到或听到的一切描述，她是一个不可小觑的人物。

sentences.en: Esther was born in 1917 in Shanghai, the daughter of a wealthy automobile importer.
sentences.zh: 埃丝特1917年出生于上海，是一位富有的汽车进口商的女儿。

sentences.en: She was well-educated and well-traveled, but in 1949 was forced to flee China to escape the
sentences.zh: 她受过良好教育，游历广泛，但在1949年被迫逃离中国以躲避

sentences.en: incoming communist regime, losing her high-end lifestyle.
sentences.zh: 即将到来的共产主义政权，失去了她高端的生活方式。

sentences.en: She made her home in Los Angeles and worked as a clerk for a shipping company for 20 years
sentences.zh: 她在洛杉矶安了家，在一家航运公司做了20年的职员，

sentences.en: before opening Madam Wong's with her husband, George.
sentences.zh: 之后才和丈夫乔治一起开了“黄夫人”。

sentences.en: Esther Wong was not interested in working with Paul, but he was insistent.
sentences.zh: 埃丝特·黄对和保罗合作不感兴趣，但他坚持不懈。

sentences.en: So I said, you know, what's your worst day?
sentences.zh: 所以我说，你知道，你生意最差的是哪天？

sentences.en: She said, Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 她说，周二。

sentences.en: I said, give me Tuesdays.
sentences.zh: 我说，把周二交给我吧。

sentences.en: After some convincing, Esther decided to let Paul experiment with their slowest days and
sentences.zh: 经过一番说服，埃丝特决定让保罗在他们生意最冷清的日子里尝试一下，

sentences.en: book some local bands.
sentences.zh: 预订一些当地乐队。

sentences.en: What Esther probably wasn't anticipating, though, was at this very time in L.A., there
sentences.zh: 然而，埃丝特可能没预料到的是，当时在洛杉矶，

sentences.en: was a rising musical scene just screaming for a new venue, punk.
sentences.zh: 有一个正在兴起的音乐场景正急需一个新的场地，那就是朋克。

sentences.en: Well, I think at the beginning, promoters felt like punk is a new thing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想起初，推广人觉得朋克是个新鲜事物。

sentences.en: And there were just a handful of places that welcomed punk with opened arms in 77.
sentences.zh: 1977年，只有少数几个地方张开双臂欢迎朋克。

sentences.en: This is Alice Bagg.
sentences.zh: 这是爱丽丝·巴格。

sentences.en: I am an old school punk rocker who started playing in a punk band in 1977.
sentences.zh: 我是一位老派朋克摇滚乐手，1977年开始在朋克乐队演奏。

sentences.en: That band she was playing in was the trailblazing first wave punk band, The Bags.
sentences.zh: 她当时所在的乐队是开创性的第一波朋克乐队——“包包乐队”。

sentences.en: In the late 70s, punk had just begun to take root in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 70年代末，朋克刚刚开始在洛杉矶扎根。

sentences.en: And Alice remembers a burgeoning scene where people like her fit in.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝记得当时有一个蓬勃发展的场景，像她这样的人都能融入其中。

sentences.en: There were a lot of bands that had women, queers, people of color.
sentences.zh: 有很多乐队里有女性、酷儿、有色人种。

sentences.en: That was very, very inclusive scene.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常、非常包容的场景。

sentences.en: And there were a lot of really unique voices.
sentences.zh: 而且有很多非常独特的声音。

sentences.en: So I think when you listen to L.A.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为当你听洛杉矶的

sentences.en: punk, it is maybe a little bit quirkier.
sentences.zh: 朋克时，它可能有点古怪。

sentences.en: But the issue was that almost no one, not the biggest arena or the smallest clubs, wanted
sentences.zh: 但问题是几乎没有人，无论是最大的竞技场还是最小的俱乐部，都想

sentences.en: to host these local bands because, well.
sentences.zh: 接待这些当地乐队，因为，嗯。

sentences.en: You know, from my personal experience, The Bags got a bad reputation for our fans being
sentences.zh: 你知道，根据我的个人经验，“包包乐队”因为粉丝太

sentences.en: too aggressive and destroying things.
sentences.zh: 激进和搞破坏而名声不好。

sentences.en: Alice isn't exaggerating about that reputation.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝关于那个名声的说法并不夸张。

sentences.en: Take, for example, in 1978, when The Bags played this very famous L.A.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，1978年，“包包乐队”在洛杉矶一家非常著名的

sentences.en: rock club called
sentences.zh: 摇滚俱乐部演出，叫

sentences.en: The Troubadour.
sentences.zh: “游吟诗人”。

sentences.en: It was later called the trashing of The Troubadour because there was a lot of craziness.
sentences.zh: 后来被称为“摧毁游吟诗人事件”，因为当时非常疯狂。

sentences.en: Rather than providing a dance floor, The Troubadour put down tables and chairs, expecting the audience
sentences.zh: “游吟诗人”没有提供舞池，而是摆放了桌椅，期望观众

sentences.en: to remain seated the whole night.
sentences.zh: 整晚都坐着。

sentences.en: And as soon as the show started, things began to go immediately awry.
sentences.zh: 演出一开始，事情立刻就乱套了。

sentences.en: If you had a punk show at one of those places and you didn't move the tables and create a
sentences.zh: 如果你在那些地方举办朋克演出，而不把桌子移开创造一个

sentences.en: dance floor, well, the punks were going to do it for you.
sentences.zh: 舞池，那么，朋克们会替你做这件事。

sentences.en: Soon enough, the audience started hurling those tables and chairs across the room.
sentences.zh: 很快，观众就开始把那些桌椅扔向房间各处。

sentences.en: You know, the furniture ended up in a pile, actually, like tables and chairs in a pile.
sentences.zh: 你知道，家具最后堆成了一堆，真的，就像桌椅堆成了一堆。

sentences.en: And there are, there's actually like video footage, I think, where you can see us playing
sentences.zh: 而且，实际上有视频片段，我想，你可以看到我们在台上演奏，

sentences.en: on stage and you see like every now and then a chair flying across.
sentences.zh: 然后时不时看到一把椅子飞过。

sentences.en: There's this photo that was taken after the chaos had subsided.
sentences.zh: 有一张照片是在混乱平息后拍摄的。

sentences.en: Wooden chairs and table pieces are strewn into a frenzied pile, as if the audience was trying
sentences.zh: 木椅和桌子的碎片散乱地堆成一堆，仿佛观众正试图

sentences.en: to barricade the place from a zombie apocalypse.
sentences.zh: 用这些东西筑起路障，抵御僵尸末日。

sentences.en: But then, of course, the bags never were, were never allowed back at The Troubadour.
sentences.zh: 但当然，后来“包包乐队”再也不被允许回到“游吟诗人”演出了。

sentences.en: And I think for a while, punk bands in general were not allowed at The Troubadours.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为有一段时间，朋克乐队通常都不被允许在“游吟诗人”演出。

sentences.en: So yes, unfortunately, these sort of things closed doors for us.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，不幸的是，这些事情为我们关上了大门。

sentences.en: It wasn't just The Troubadour banning punk bands.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是“游吟诗人”禁止朋克乐队。

sentences.en: It was most clubs.
sentences.zh: 大多数俱乐部都这样。

sentences.en: So punks had to make do.
sentences.zh: 所以朋克们不得不凑合着过。

sentences.en: They'd try sliding in through the back door of alternative, unsuspecting venues.
sentences.zh: 他们会尝试从那些另类、毫无防备的场地的后门溜进去。

sentences.en: Some bands would book shows in abandoned synagogues or Ukrainian cultural centers or the performance
sentences.zh: 有些乐队会在废弃的犹太教堂、乌克兰文化中心或“麋鹿慈善保护协会”的表演厅

sentences.en: hall of the Benevolent and Protective Order of the Elks.
sentences.zh: 预订演出。

sentences.en: But as soon as the establishment figured out what was happening, they'd pull the plug or
sentences.zh: 但一旦当权者发现发生了什么，他们就会切断电源或

sentences.en: call the cops.
sentences.zh: 报警。

sentences.en: The plan for Madam Wong's was to book all types of music, not just punk rock.
sentences.zh: “黄夫人”的计划是预订各种类型的音乐，而不仅仅是朋克摇滚。

sentences.en: But by opening her club up to the scene, Esther Wong was about to form an uneasy alliance with
sentences.zh: 但通过向这个圈子开放她的俱乐部，埃丝特·黄即将与

sentences.en: the punks knocking at her door.
sentences.zh: 敲她门的朋克们结成一种不安的联盟。

sentences.en: Paul jumped in immediately and designed flyers and posters and stapled them to telephone poles
sentences.zh: 保罗立即行动起来，设计了传单和海报，并把它们钉在全城的

sentences.en: all over town.
sentences.zh: 电线杆上。

sentences.en: After a few months of planning, Paul kicked off the weeknight shows in the fall of 1978
sentences.zh: 经过几个月的筹划，保罗在1978年秋天开始了工作日的演出，

sentences.en: with a musician named Gary Valentine.
sentences.zh: 邀请了一位名叫加里·瓦伦丁的音乐人。

sentences.en: You know, in the beginning, it was really, and Madam Wong's, it was very exciting.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在开始的时候，真的，在“黄夫人”，那非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: I mean, I wish I had kept a bottle of the adrenaline that I got every night out of that
sentences.zh: 我是说，我真希望我能留住一瓶我每天晚上从那个

sentences.en: place.
sentences.zh: 地方获得的肾上腺素。

sentences.en: Madam Wong's featured different types of music, but the punks were the ones who really turned

sentences.en: And so the Chinese-American merchants are trying to make Chinese-American difference palatable
sentences.zh: 所以美籍华裔商人们试图让美籍华裔的独特性变得更符合

sentences.en: So in the late 1970s, decades after new Chinatown drew in outsiders with its deliberate
sentences.zh: 因此在 20 世纪 70 年代末，在新唐人街凭借其刻意的

sentences.en: chinoiserie, Esther and George Wong did something similar.
sentences.zh: 中国风设计吸引外来者几十年后，Esther 和 George Wong 做了类似的事情。

sentences.en: They capitalized on a new crowd by selling them an experience they couldn't get anywhere else.
sentences.zh: 他们通过向新客群出售一种在别处无法获得的体验，从中获利。

sentences.en: If you have Chinese-American businesses whose lifeblood are people outside of the community,
sentences.zh: 如果你经营的美籍华裔企业，其命脉是社区之外的人，

sentences.zh: 那么朋克圈子也不过是其中的另一个侧面而已。

sentences.zh: 这是那种共生关系更广泛历史的一部分，

sentences.zh: 在这种关系中，美籍华裔企业迎合了那些

sentences.en: Despite what the media had dubbed her, other punks like Alice knew that there was a different story there.
sentences.zh: 尽管媒体给她冠上了这个头衔，但像爱丽丝这样的朋克乐手都知道，事实并非如此。

sentences.en: I don't think she deserves to be called anything that would frame her in terms of supporting punk.
sentences.zh: 我不认为她配得上任何将她与支持朋克联系在一起的称呼。

sentences.en: Maybe, you know, that could be adjusted to new wave, but not punk.
sentences.zh: 也许，你知道，这可以调整为新浪潮，但绝不是朋克。

sentences.en: Around the time that Esther discovered rock in the late 1970s, punk music was changing, and a new style was splintering out into its own separate genre, new wave.
sentences.zh: 在埃丝特于70年代末发现摇滚乐时，朋克音乐正在发生变化，一种新的风格正逐渐分化为一个独立的流派——新浪潮。

sentences.en: New wave is a lot like punk, if you added ironic lyrics, mainstream appeal, and a couple of synthesizers.
sentences.zh: 如果你在新浪潮中加入讽刺的歌词、主流的吸引力以及几台合成器，它就和朋克很像了。

sentences.en: To many punks, the distinction between the two genres meant everything.
sentences.zh: 对许多朋克乐手来说，这两个流派之间的区别至关重要。

sentences.en: But to Esther Wong, these subtle musical differences weren't enough for her to put up with the rowdy punk crowd.
sentences.zh: 但对埃丝特·王来说，这些细微的音乐差异并不足以让她去忍受那些吵闹的朋克人群。

sentences.en: So as business began picking up, Esther pivoted and focused on booking new wave over punk.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着生意好转，埃丝特转变了策略，专注于预订新浪潮乐队而非朋克乐队。

sentences.en: The new wavers tended to act a little more professionally and draw in slightly tamer audiences.
sentences.zh: 新浪潮乐手通常表现得更专业一些，吸引的观众也稍微温和一点。

sentences.en: My guess is Ongo Bongo probably didn't tag Esther's bathroom.
sentences.zh: 我猜Ongo Bongo乐队大概不会去涂鸦埃丝特的洗手间。

sentences.en: I am pretty sure that our first show in Chinatown was at Madam Wong's, and it was also our last show at Madam Wong's.
sentences.zh: 我很确定我们在唐人街的第一场演出是在王夫人餐厅，那也是我们在那里的最后一场演出。

sentences.en: Alice says that the bag's first show at Madam Wong's ended a lot like the trashing of the troubadour.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝说，巴格乐队在王夫人餐厅的首演，结局和特罗巴多酒吧那次被砸场子差不多。

sentences.en: Things got out of hand, and a lot of furniture got damaged.
sentences.zh: 场面失控了，很多家具都被损坏了。

sentences.en: Esther got tired of this sort of thing, and began straight up banning a lot of punk bands.
sentences.zh: 埃丝特厌倦了这种事，开始直接封杀很多朋克乐队。

sentences.en: So punk had to find another venue, and lucky for us, the Hong Kong Cafe opened.
sentences.zh: 所以朋克们不得不寻找另一个场地，幸运的是，香港咖啡馆开业了。

sentences.en: After the break, the Hong Kong Cafe opens, and the Chinatown punk wars begin.
sentences.zh: 休息过后，香港咖啡馆开业，唐人街的朋克战争开始了。

sentences.en: In 1979, less than a year after Esther and George began booking rock shows at Madam Wong's,
sentences.zh: 1979年，在埃丝特和乔治开始在王夫人餐厅预订摇滚演出不到一年后，

sentences.en: a different music promoter happened to find himself in Chinatown.
sentences.zh: 一位不同的音乐推广人恰好来到了唐人街。

sentences.en: His name was Kim Turner.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫金·特纳。

sentences.en: Well, I was looking for a place from the minute I got here.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我从到这儿的第一分钟起就在找地方。

sentences.en: Kim was fresh off the plane from D.C.
sentences.zh: 金刚从华盛顿飞抵这里，

sentences.en: and already looking for a space to run shows out of.
sentences.zh: 就已经在寻找可以举办演出的场地了。

sentences.en: One night, he went to Madam Wong's in Chinatown,
sentences.zh: 一天晚上，他去了唐人街的王夫人餐厅，

sentences.en: and he thought that Central Plaza, with its neon lights and architecture,
sentences.zh: 他觉得中央广场凭借其霓虹灯和建筑风格，

sentences.en: should have more than just one single rock club.
sentences.zh: 不应该只有一个摇滚俱乐部。

sentences.en: It had the potential to be an entire music scene.
sentences.zh: 它有潜力成为一个完整的音乐场景。

sentences.en: So as he was walking out of Madam Wong's, he got an idea.
sentences.zh: 所以当他走出王夫人餐厅时，他产生了一个想法。

sentences.en: I came down the stairs, and I looked across the way there,
sentences.zh: 我走下楼梯，看向对面，

sentences.en: and I saw the Hong Kong Low restaurant.
sentences.zh: 我看到了香港楼餐厅。

sentences.en: I go, wow, that would be a perfect place for a band, for a nightclub.
sentences.zh: 我说，哇，那将是一个完美的乐队演出场地，一个夜店。

sentences.en: Kim saw that literally steps away from Madam Wong's.
sentences.zh: 金发现，就在离王夫人餐厅几步之遥的地方，

sentences.en: There just happened to be another struggling Chinese restaurant,
sentences.zh: 刚好有另一家中餐馆经营困难，

sentences.en: big enough to host the shows he had in mind.
sentences.zh: 规模大到足以举办他心目中的演出。

sentences.en: It was called Hong Kong Low.
sentences.zh: 它叫香港楼。

sentences.en: So I went over and I talked to, I introduced myself to Bill Hong.
sentences.zh: 所以我走过去，和比尔·洪聊了聊，做了自我介绍。

sentences.en: We sat down and talked.
sentences.zh: 我们坐下来谈了谈。

sentences.en: Bill Hong had been the owner of Hong Kong Low for decades,
sentences.zh: 比尔·洪经营香港楼已经几十年了，

sentences.en: and was a prominent and well-liked member of the Chinatown community.
sentences.zh: 是唐人街社区中一位杰出且广受好评的成员。

sentences.en: He was the executive secretary of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce,
sentences.zh: 他是中华总商会的执行秘书，

sentences.en: where he helped new immigrants settle in Chinatown in the early 70s.
sentences.zh: 在70年代初，他曾帮助新移民在唐人街安顿下来。

sentences.en: He also helped organize the annual Lunar New Year parade.
sentences.zh: 他还协助组织了每年的农历新年游行。

sentences.en: What was his personality like?
sentences.zh: 他的性格怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm just kind of curious.
sentences.zh: 我只是有点好奇。

sentences.en: He was very, I don't know, he ran a good business.
sentences.zh: 他非常……我不知道，他生意做得很好。

sentences.en: Well, you saw it in one picture of him at that scene, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你在那张现场照片里看到他了，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, that was a good description of him.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是对他的一个很好的描述。

sentences.en: Kim was referring to a photo of Bill that he'd sent me before our interview.
sentences.zh: 金指的是他在我们采访前发给我的一张比尔的照片。

sentences.en: Bill's holding up a lobster that he had just pulled out of Hong Kong Low's live seafood tank.
sentences.zh: 比尔手里拿着一只刚从香港楼活海鲜缸里捞出来的龙虾。

sentences.en: He's wearing a bow tie and has this huge, playful grin across his round face.
sentences.zh: 他戴着领结，圆圆的脸上挂着灿烂而顽皮的笑容。

sentences.en: He looks like a sweet, happy dad.
sentences.zh: 他看起来像个可爱、快乐的父亲。

sentences.en: No one I spoke with had a single bad thing to say about him.
sentences.zh: 我采访过的所有人对他都没有一句坏话。

sentences.en: And luckily for Kim, Bill was open to turning Hong Kong Low into Chinatown's second rock club.
sentences.zh: 对金来说幸运的是，比尔愿意把香港楼变成唐人街的第二个摇滚俱乐部。

sentences.en: I said, well, let me get back with you.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，让我再联系你。

sentences.en: I'll come back tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我明天再来。

sentences.en: He said, yeah, we'll do this.
sentences.zh: 他说，好，我们就这么办。

sentences.en: Hong Kong Low was a large two-story building.
sentences.zh: 香港楼是一栋大型的两层建筑。

sentences.en: On the ground floor was the main dining area.
sentences.zh: 一楼是主要的用餐区。

sentences.en: And on the second floor was a private banquet room that Bill booked out for buffets and special events.
sentences.zh: 二楼是一个私人宴会厅，比尔通常把它租出去举办自助餐和特别活动。

sentences.en: The banquet room was mostly unused.
sentences.zh: 宴会厅大部分时间都闲置着。

sentences.en: And their idea was to convert that space into a new club called the Hong Kong Cafe.
sentences.zh: 他们的想法是将那个空间改造成一个名为“香港咖啡馆”的新俱乐部。

sentences.en: Kim brought on two other partners, a woman named Susie Frank who died in 2022 and a man named Barry Seidel.
sentences.zh: 金找了另外两个合伙人，一位名叫苏西·弗兰克的女士（已于2022年去世）和一位名叫巴里·塞德尔的男士。

sentences.en: We opened that club not knowing that we were going to be a premier punk club.
sentences.zh: 我们开那家俱乐部时，并不知道我们会成为顶级的朋克俱乐部。

sentences.en: We did not know that.
sentences.zh: 我们当时不知道。

sentences.en: This is Barry Seidel.
sentences.zh: 这位是巴里·塞德尔。

sentences.en: Like Esther Wong, Barry did not originally set out to be a champion for punk music.
sentences.zh: 和埃丝特·王一样，巴里最初也没打算成为朋克音乐的捍卫者。

sentences.en: But he and Kim had overheard the angry grumblings of punk bands who had been booted out of Madam Wong's,
sentences.zh: 但他和金听到了那些被王夫人餐厅赶出来的朋克乐队愤怒的抱怨，

sentences.en: and they saw an opportunity.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了机会。

sentences.en: As soon as we opened, we realized that we had an enemy next door that was threatening all the bands.
sentences.zh: 我们一开业就意识到，隔壁有个敌人正在威胁所有的乐队。

sentences.en: So then we started to become aware of, oh God, so many punk bands that were not being used.
sentences.zh: 于是我们开始意识到，天哪，有那么多朋克乐队没地方去。

sentences.en: People were afraid of them.
sentences.zh: 人们都怕他们。

sentences.en: And we figured, what the hell?
sentences.zh: 我们想，管他呢？

sentences.en: We could really do something with these bands if we can get by with it, if we can handle it.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能应付得来，如果我们能处理好，我们真的能利用这些乐队做点什么。

sentences.en: Barry and Kim built a stage from scratch and published a press release for the official June 5th, 1979 opening of the brand new Hong Kong Cafe.
sentences.zh: 巴里和金从零开始搭建了一个舞台，并为1979年6月5日正式开业的全新香港咖啡馆发布了新闻稿。

sentences.en: It advertised the best in rock, live seafood, and live entertainment.
sentences.zh: 广告宣传的是最好的摇滚乐、活海鲜和现场娱乐表演。

sentences.en: And every choice that Madam Wong's made, the guys at the Hong Kong purposely went the other direction.
sentences.zh: 而且王夫人餐厅做的每一个选择，香港咖啡馆的人都故意反着来。

sentences.en: Esther made Madam Wong's 21 and up, so the Hong Kong was all ages.
sentences.zh: 埃丝特规定王夫人餐厅只接待21岁以上的客人，所以香港咖啡馆欢迎所有年龄段的人。

sentences.en: If Madam Wong's was going to cast out the unruly punk bands, the Hong Kong would take them in.
sentences.zh: 如果王夫人餐厅要驱逐那些不守规矩的朋克乐队，香港咖啡馆就会接纳他们。

sentences.en: Even if they were trouble.
sentences.zh: 即使他们是麻烦制造者。

sentences.en: The first night that we were running a big punk show, everybody said, watch out for Black Randy.
sentences.zh: 我们举办大型朋克演出的第一晚，每个人都说，小心“黑兰迪”。

sentences.en: I said, what's that?
sentences.zh: 我说，那是什么？

sentences.en: They were referring to Black Randy and the Metro Squad.
sentences.zh: 他们指的是“黑兰迪与地铁小队”乐队。

sentences.en: You know, I'm new in L.A.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我是刚到洛杉矶的，

sentences.en: here, you know.
sentences.zh: 在这儿，你知道的。

sentences.en: They said, well, just watch out for Black Randy, he's a toilet breaker.
sentences.zh: 他们说，嗯，小心黑兰迪就行，他是“碎厕者”。

sentences.en: I said, what's a toilet breaker?
sentences.zh: 我说，什么是“碎厕者”？

sentences.en: That one actually turned out to be pretty self-explanatory.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这个词本身就解释了一切。

sentences.en: So the night's over, the toilet's broken.
sentences.zh: 演出结束了，厕所也碎了。

sentences.en: Water all over the place.
sentences.zh: 到处都是水。

sentences.en: So that was one of the first lessons that we had.
sentences.zh: 所以那是我们学到的第一课之一。

sentences.en: And if you're listening, Randy, we're on to you.
sentences.zh: 如果你在听的话，兰迪，我们盯上你了。

sentences.en: The shows took a toll on the Hong Kong Cafe.
sentences.zh: 这些演出给香港咖啡馆带来了损失。

sentences.en: But Barry, Kim, and Bill eventually worked out a deal that any damage done to the club would be taken out of the band's cut of the night.
sentences.zh: 但巴里、金和比尔最终达成了一项协议：对俱乐部造成的任何损坏都将从乐队当晚的收入中扣除。

sentences.en: Bill was kind of a happy-go-lucky guy.
sentences.zh: 比尔是个乐天派。

sentences.en: You know, when he was picking up bottles, you know, in the plaza.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当他在广场上捡瓶子的时候，

sentences.en: He always had a smile.
sentences.zh: 他总是面带微笑。

sentences.en: He always had a little chuckle.
sentences.zh: 他总是会发出一点轻笑。

sentences.en: And he said, hey, it's kind of like maybe a cost of doing business.
sentences.zh: 他说，嘿，这就像是做生意的成本吧。

sentences.en: This is Ken Chan.
sentences.zh: 这位是肯·陈。

sentences.en: His family owns Phoenix Bakery, which is a business that's been in Chinatown for over 80 years.
sentences.zh: 他的家族拥有凤凰饼家，这是一家在唐人街经营了80多年的企业。

sentences.en: He says that, in the beginning, both Esther and Bill got some pushback from the local community because of some vandalism.
sentences.zh: 他说，起初，埃丝特和比尔都因为一些破坏行为而受到当地社区的抵制。

sentences.en: But Esther and Bill stuck up for the shows.
sentences.zh: 但埃丝特和比尔坚持支持这些演出。

sentences.en: There was some vandalism.
sentences.zh: 确实有一些破坏行为。

sentences.en: There was some trash.
sentences.zh: 确实有一些垃圾。

sentences.en: You know, every night Bill would go out there with a broom and he started swooping up stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道，每天晚上比尔都会拿着扫帚出去清扫东西。

sentences.en: Bill would tell me, hey, you know, I got to keep the place up and running.
sentences.zh: 比尔会告诉我，嘿，你知道，我得让这地方维持运转。

sentences.en: I got to pay my rent.
sentences.zh: 我得付房租。

sentences.en: I got to pay my staff.
sentences.zh: 我得付员工工资。

sentences.en: The shows and audiences could get chaotic, but it was all worth it to draw bigger crowds into Central Plaza.
sentences.zh: 演出和观众可能会变得混乱，但为了吸引更多人流进入中央广场，这一切都是值得的。

sentences.en: Bigger crowds meant more money spent at the bar and in the restaurant, which went straight to Bill.
sentences.zh: 更多的人流意味着在酒吧和餐厅有更多的消费，而这些钱直接进了比尔的口袋。

sentences.en: We were both helping each other out.
sentences.zh: 我们都在互相帮助。

sentences.en: He was giving us a place to do our business.
sentences.zh: 他为我们提供了做生意的场地。

sentences.en: And he was doing well with all the people, you know, coming in.
sentences.zh: 而且他通过这些进来的人赚了不少钱，你知道的。

sentences.en: And not only would they go down and eat dinner downstairs, but then they would come upstairs and drink, too, you know, and watch the bands.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅会去楼下吃晚饭，还会上楼喝酒，你知道，顺便看乐队演出。

sentences.en: And although it was mainly a business decision for Bill, the Hong Kong cafe ended up becoming hugely important to the punk scene.
sentences.zh: 虽然这对比尔来说主要是一个商业决定，但香港咖啡馆最终对朋克圈变得极其重要。

sentences.en: It gave a forum to people that might have a difficult time finding a place to perform.
sentences.zh: 它为那些难以找到表演场所的人提供了一个平台。

sentences.en: Here's Alice Bag again.
sentences.zh: 又是爱丽丝·巴格。

sentences.en: She appreciated that the Hong Kong was a place where artistic expression could run rampant.
sentences.zh: 她很感激香港咖啡馆是一个可以让艺术表达肆意发挥的地方。

sentences.en: People like her had the freedom to get weird and experimental on stage.
sentences.zh: 像她这样的人有自由在舞台上变得怪异和实验性。

sentences.en: I just wanted to say that one of the most impactful shows that I saw at the Hong Kong cafe was Joanna Wendt.
sentences.zh: 我只想说，我在香港咖啡馆看过的最具冲击力的演出之一是乔安娜·温特的表演。

sentences.en: Have you ever heard of Joanna Wendt?
sentences.zh: 你听说过乔安娜·温特吗？

sentences.en: Here's Barry again.
sentences.zh: 又是巴里。

sentences.en: He remembers this show very well.
sentences.zh: 他清楚地记得这场演出。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Joanna came to me and she wanted to play the Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 乔安娜来找我，说她想在香港咖啡馆演出。

sentences.en: Well, she's a performance artist and she does weird stuff.
sentences.zh: 嗯，她是一位行为艺术家，她做的事情很怪。

sentences.en: So I said, I said, what do you do?
sentences.zh: 所以我问，我说，你表演什么？

sentences.en: And as far as I can remember, word for word, she said, well, first, I cover the stage with a plastic sheet and and there's a lot of blood and it's kind of messy.
sentences.zh: 据我记忆，她一字不差地说，嗯，首先，我会用塑料布铺满舞台，会有很多血，有点乱。

sentences.en: But I clean up afterwards.
sentences.zh: 但我事后会清理干净。

sentences.en: You can watch some of Joanna Wendt's work online.
sentences.zh: 你可以在网上看到一些乔安娜·温特的作品。

sentences.en: And to be honest, it will probably you up a little bit.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这可能会让你有点反胃。

sentences.en: But to her credit, she did clean up afterwards.
sentences.zh: 但值得称赞的是，她确实事后清理干净了。

sentences.en: You know, that's something that made the Hong Kong cafe really unique,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这让香港咖啡馆变得非常独特，

sentences.en: like that it would host a performance artist that was known for like being a little bit out of control for using stuff like that would get on the furniture, get on the floor,
sentences.zh: 因为它会接待一位以失控著称的行为艺术家，她会把东西弄到家具上、地板上，

sentences.en: get on the customers.
sentences.zh: 弄到顾客身上。

sentences.en: And they weren't afraid of that.
sentences.zh: 而他们并不害怕这一点。

sentences.en: And the blood-soaked shows were blowing up.
sentences.zh: 那些血淋淋的演出火爆异常。

sentences.en: Kids who were turned away at the door were scaling the roof and breaking in through the air conditioning ducts.
sentences.zh: 被拒之门外的孩子们会爬上屋顶，从空调管道钻进来。

sentences.en: Kim Turner told me that one time a person was so desperate to get into a show that he fell through the vent and nearly impaled himself on the drummer's hi-hat.
sentences.zh: 金·特纳告诉我，有一次一个人为了看演出太拼命，结果从通风口掉了下来，差点被鼓手的镲片刺穿。

sentences.en: And it wasn't just punks.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是朋克乐手。

sentences.en: All sorts of people heard the buzz around the Hong Kong cafe and started showing up in Central Plaza.
sentences.zh: 各种各样的人都听说了香港咖啡馆的热度，开始出现在中央广场。

sentences.en: John Belushi used to come in all the time.
sentences.zh: 约翰·贝鲁西以前经常来。

sentences.en: And also Donna Summer became a friend of mine.
sentences.zh: 还有唐娜·萨默也成了我的朋友。

sentences.en: She's very small.
sentences.zh: 她个子非常小。

sentences.en: And she loved the Hong Kong cafe.
sentences.zh: 而且她很喜欢这家香港咖啡馆。

sentences.en: And she would come in and I'd say, Donna, you must wear this hat and go sit in that corner.
sentences.zh: 她会走进来，然后我对她说：唐娜，你一定要戴上这顶帽子，去那个角落坐着。

sentences.en: Because if they knew that was Donna Summer, they would have ripped her apart.
sentences.zh: 因为如果他们知道那是唐娜·莎曼，他们会把她团团围住的。

sentences.en: The disco queen, you know.
sentences.zh: 毕竟是迪斯科女王，你懂的。

sentences.en: Night after night, punk bands kept the second floor of Hong Kong Lowe's packed.
sentences.zh: 夜复一夜，朋克乐队让香港咖啡馆的二楼总是挤得满满当当。

sentences.en: Maybe even too packed.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能挤得过头了。

sentences.en: The place wasn't that big.
sentences.zh: 那个地方其实没那么大。

sentences.en: I think the legal crowd in there was only 250.
sentences.zh: 我想那里的合法容纳人数只有250人。

sentences.en: And we would put maybe 400 people in there.
sentences.zh: 但我们有时会塞进400人左右。

sentences.en: And downstairs in the restaurant, I used to get scared because you could look up at the ceiling.
sentences.zh: 楼下的餐厅里，我以前常感到害怕，因为你可以抬头看到天花板。

sentences.en: And when there was like 400 people in there jumping around and doing a mosh pit and everything else going on,
sentences.zh: 当里面有四百来号人在那儿蹦蹦跳跳、搞冲撞舞池，还有其他各种动静时，

sentences.en: you could see the ceiling just kind of bouncing up and down.
sentences.zh: 你能看到天花板就在那儿上下晃动。

sentences.en: You know, it's kind of scary.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那挺吓人的。

sentences.en: We got busted by the fire department many times for overcrowding.
sentences.zh: 我们因为超员被消防部门查处过很多次。

sentences.en: Madam Wong probably called them.
sentences.zh: 大概是黄太太报的警。

sentences.en: One person who was not a fan of the Hong Kong's chaotic, punk-loving vibe was Esther Wong.
sentences.zh: 埃丝特·黄就是那个不喜欢香港咖啡馆那种混乱、热爱朋克氛围的人。

sentences.en: She would be sitting because both clubs were on the second level.
sentences.zh: 她会坐在那儿，因为两家俱乐部都在二楼。

sentences.en: This is Kim Turner again, Barry's other partner at the Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 这是金·特纳，巴里在香港咖啡馆的另一位合伙人。

sentences.en: And you could see her behind her bars looking, you know, with her binoculars into our club, seeing what was going on.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到她坐在吧台后面，用望远镜盯着我们的俱乐部，看里面在搞什么名堂。

sentences.en: In the beginning, Esther was actually quoted in the L.A.
sentences.zh: 起初，埃丝特甚至在《洛杉矶时报》上公开表示，

sentences.en: Times welcoming the competition in Chinatown.
sentences.zh: 欢迎唐人街出现竞争。

sentences.en: But that attitude quickly changed.
sentences.zh: 但那种态度很快就变了。

sentences.en: She didn't talk very openly about why she didn't like the Hong Kong Cafe.
sentences.zh: 她并没有公开谈论过为什么不喜欢香港咖啡馆。

sentences.en: So it was assumed that it was just sheer territorialism on her part.
sentences.zh: 所以人们推测这纯粹是她的领地意识在作祟。

sentences.en: But it went deeper than that.
sentences.zh: 但事情远不止于此。

sentences.en: I think she felt like there was a rivalry and like the Hong Kong Cafe's like sort of culture was disrespectful to her.
sentences.zh: 我觉得她认为这是一种竞争，而且觉得香港咖啡馆那种文化对她不尊重。

sentences.en: As far as I know, Esther didn't have a problem with Bill Hong.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，埃丝特和比尔·洪之间没什么矛盾。

sentences.en: But she was not a fan of Barry and Kim.
sentences.zh: 但她不喜欢巴里和金。

sentences.en: It may have all started when Barry took out an ad in the Weekly promoting the opening of the Hong Kong Cafe.
sentences.zh: 这一切可能始于巴里在《周刊》上刊登了一则广告，宣传香港咖啡馆的开业。

sentences.en: Barry took a swipe at Madam Wong's by writing,
sentences.zh: 巴里写道，以此嘲讽了黄太太的店：

sentences.en: You've tried the first and fineSt. Now try the biggest and the beSt.
sentences.zh: 你已经尝试过第一和最好的了，现在来试试最大和最棒的吧。

sentences.en: I thought it was very funny.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很有趣。

sentences.en: She did not like that stuff at all.
sentences.zh: 但她一点也不喜欢那一套。

sentences.en: It then snowballed when Esther's then promoter instituted a three to four week cooling period for bands that played the Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 随后矛盾升级，埃丝特当时的经纪人规定，在香港咖啡馆演出过的乐队必须有三到四周的冷却期。

sentences.en: To them, it just made business sense that they wouldn't want to book a band that had just played the venue 30 yards away the night before.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，这纯粹是商业考量，他们不想预订一支前一天刚在30码外演出过的乐队。

sentences.en: But most people interpreted this as a blanket ban on any band that played the Hong Kong Cafe.
sentences.zh: 但大多数人将其解读为对任何在香港咖啡馆演出过的乐队的全面封杀。

sentences.en: This policy, along with the fact that Esther stopped booking punk bands, gave her a reputation for being vindictive.
sentences.zh: 这项政策，加上埃丝特停止预订朋克乐队的事实，让她落下了记仇的名声。

sentences.en: It also drew a line in the sand in Central Plaza.
sentences.zh: 这也让中央广场划出了一道界线。

sentences.en: On one side of the courtyard was Esther Wong and her skinny tie-wearing New Wave bands.
sentences.zh: 庭院的一边是埃丝特·黄和她那些戴着窄领带的新浪潮乐队。

sentences.en: And on the other was the Hong Kong and the punks.
sentences.zh: 另一边则是香港咖啡馆和朋克们。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, they were like steps away from each other, like kitty corner, right?
sentences.zh: 是啊，我是说，他们离得只有几步之遥，就像是对角线一样，对吧？

sentences.en: And very, very, very close.
sentences.zh: 而且非常、非常、非常近。

sentences.en: So you can actually see like, you know, the New Wave audience lined up for a show at Madam Wong's.
sentences.zh: 所以你实际上可以看到，你知道，新浪潮的观众在黄太太店外排队等演出。

sentences.en: And like the punk rock audience lined up at the Hong Kong Cafe.
sentences.zh: 而朋克摇滚的观众在香港咖啡馆外排队。

sentences.en: The L.A.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶的

sentences.en: press got wind of this tension in Chinatown and stoked the flames of the feud.
sentences.zh: 媒体嗅到了唐人街的这种紧张气氛，并煽风点火。

sentences.en: The local media gave the whole clash an unfortunate nickname.
sentences.zh: 当地媒体给这场冲突起了一个不幸的绰号。

sentences.en: I guess we're going to get into the Wonton Wars now.
sentences.zh: 我想我们现在要谈谈“馄饨战争”了。

sentences.en: I might as well, right?
sentences.zh: 反正也绕不开，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, the Wonton Wars.
sentences.zh: 没错，馄饨战争。

sentences.en: It was also dubbed the Chinatown Syndrome and then, thank God, later just referred to as the Chinatown Punk Wars.
sentences.zh: 它还被称为“唐人街综合症”，后来，谢天谢地，简称为“唐人街朋克战争”。

sentences.en: Barry openly admits that the war between the Hong Kong and Madam Wong's was ginned up by the media.
sentences.zh: 巴里公开承认，香港咖啡馆和黄太太店之间的战争是媒体炒作出来的。

sentences.en: The tall tale of these two warring restaurants was media gold.
sentences.zh: 这两家餐厅交战的传奇故事简直是媒体的摇钱树。

sentences.en: But the press also recast the godmother of punk into a new role.
sentences.zh: 但媒体也将这位“朋克教母”重塑成了一个新角色。

sentences.en: Because like every good story, the Chinatown Punk Wars had to have good guys and bad guys.
sentences.zh: 因为就像所有好故事一样，唐人街朋克战争必须有正面人物和反面人物。

sentences.en: And the villain was an obvious choice.
sentences.zh: 而反派是一个显而易见的选择。

sentences.en: So, when the press would hear something that she would say or complain about, which was a lot of things, I guess, they would come running in.
sentences.zh: 所以，当媒体听到她说的话或抱怨时——我想那可多了去了——他们就会跑过来。

sentences.en: They would take her story.
sentences.zh: 他们会采用她的说法。

sentences.en: Then they'd come to me.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会来找我。

sentences.en: And I, of course, was the nice guy from New York that everybody loved.
sentences.zh: 而我，当然，就是那个大家都喜欢的来自纽约的好人。

sentences.en: And I, anybody can play the Hong Kong, you know.
sentences.zh: 而且我，谁都能在香港咖啡馆演出，你知道的。

sentences.en: He says that he remembered journalists telling him that when they came to do stories about the Hong Kong at the time, they would photograph him in flattering ways.
sentences.zh: 他说他记得记者告诉他，当他们当时来做关于香港咖啡馆的报道时，他们会以讨好的方式拍摄他。

sentences.en: They'd stage him with flowers and potted plants to make him look endearing, like a harmless woodland creature.
sentences.zh: 他们会用花卉和盆栽来衬托他，让他看起来很可爱，就像某种无害的森林小动物。

sentences.en: But on the flip side with Esther.
sentences.zh: 但反过来对待埃丝特时。

sentences.en: They would shoot her from the ground up.
sentences.zh: 他们会从下往上仰拍她。

sentences.en: They told me that that's what they would do because it made her look like evil.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我他们之所以这么做，是因为这让她看起来很邪恶。

sentences.en: The Chinatown Punk Wars generated a lot of attention for the Hong Kong Cafe.
sentences.zh: 唐人街朋克战争为香港咖啡馆带来了极大的关注。

sentences.en: And Barry says, at times, he even took advantage of this dynamic.
sentences.zh: 巴里说，有时他甚至会利用这种动态。

sentences.en: Whenever Madame Wong was not complaining, it was not good for business.
sentences.zh: 每当黄太太不抱怨的时候，生意就不太好。

sentences.en: So we would do something to make her complain.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会做点什么让她抱怨。

sentences.en: And then we would just, I didn't know, I didn't do it.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就装傻，我不知道，我没做过。

sentences.en: I don't know what she's talking about, you know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道她在说什么，你知道的。

sentences.en: The most infamous example of this was an elaborate prank called the Trojan Tape.
sentences.zh: 这方面最臭名昭著的例子是一个叫“特洛伊木马磁带”的精心恶作剧。

sentences.en: The story involved a musician named Dwight Twilley, who was releasing a new album.
sentences.zh: 故事涉及一位名叫德怀特·特威利的音乐家，他当时正在发行新专辑。

sentences.en: At the time, clubs like Madame Wong's had sound guys who played cassettes over the speakers in between musical acts so the audience would have something to listen to.
sentences.zh: 那时，像黄太太店这样的俱乐部都有音响师，会在演出间隙播放磁带，好让观众有东西听。

sentences.en: And with Dwight Twilley's new album coming out that week, Barry got an idea.
sentences.zh: 随着德怀特·特威利的新专辑在那周发行，巴里想到了一个主意。

sentences.en: What we did is, I got my friend Kenny, who does a little disc jockey kind of thing as a joke all the time.
sentences.zh: 我们做的是，我找了我的朋友肯尼，他平时总喜欢开玩笑做点DJ之类的事。

sentences.en: So I said, come on, Kenny, listen, we're going to get the Dwight Twilley tape and very carefully open the cellophane, open the tape, and then you go to like the second cut.
sentences.zh: 所以我说，来吧，肯尼，听着，我们要拿到德怀特·特威利的磁带，小心翼翼地拆开玻璃纸，打开磁带，然后你跳到第二首曲子那里。

sentences.en: A few minutes into the cassette, Barry and his friend recorded a secret message, resealed the tape, and then sent it to Esther along with a forged note from Twilley.
sentences.zh: 在磁带播放几分钟后，巴里和他的朋友录下了一条秘密信息，重新封好磁带，并附上一张伪造的特威利便条寄给了埃丝特。

sentences.en: Sure enough, thinking that it was a promotional gift, Esther's sound person played the cassette in the club that night.
sentences.zh: 果然，埃丝特的音响师以为这是促销礼品，那天晚上就在俱乐部里播放了这盘磁带。

sentences.en: And halfway through track two, the music cut out and a voice said,
sentences.zh: 当第二首歌放到一半时，音乐突然中断，一个声音说道：

sentences.en: Come on over to the Hong Kong, it's the best place in Chinatown, just a couple of hops and jumps away from you, from where you are, you know, whatever.
sentences.zh: 来香港咖啡馆吧，这是唐人街最好的地方，离你现在的地方只有几步之遥，你知道的，随便吧。

sentences.en: Anyway, I had a lot of fun with that.
sentences.zh: 总之，我玩得很开心。

sentences.en: So did the press.
sentences.zh: 媒体也是。

sentences.en: They liked it.
sentences.zh: 他们很喜欢。

sentences.en: But Esther Wong did not.
sentences.zh: 但埃丝特·黄不喜欢。

sentences.en: According to witnesses that night, Esther was fuming and lost it in front of the entire club.
sentences.zh: 据当晚的目击者称，埃丝特当时气疯了，在整个俱乐部面前大发雷霆。

sentences.en: Barry had lots of stories like the Trojan tape.
sentences.zh: 巴里有很多像“特洛伊木马磁带”这样的故事。

sentences.en: As you could tell, he had a lot of fun with the Chinatown punk wars.
sentences.zh: 如你所见，他在唐人街朋克战争中玩得很开心。

sentences.en: Unlike Esther, he always came out on the other side unscathed.
sentences.zh: 和埃丝特不同，他总是能全身而退。

sentences.en: Like, Madam Wong was the nasty club owner, and Barry Seidel and Kim, we were the nice guys from the East Coast that didn't want to hurt anybody.
sentences.zh: 就像，黄太太是那个讨厌的俱乐部老板，而巴里·塞德尔和金，我们是来自东海岸的好人，不想伤害任何人。

sentences.en: We just wanted to be good guys, you know.
sentences.zh: 我们只是想做个好人，你知道的。

sentences.en: And that's the way it played.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样发展的。

sentences.en: But some of the things we did to her behind the scenes to make her keep going, because she was serious.
sentences.zh: 但我们私下里对她做的一些事是为了让她继续折腾，因为她是认真的。

sentences.en: We knew it was funny.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这很有趣。

sentences.en: She did not.
sentences.zh: 她却不觉得。

sentences.en: It wasn't funny to Esther, because she and Barry were very different people with very different stakes.
sentences.zh: 这对埃丝特来说一点也不好笑，因为她和巴里是截然不同的人，有着截然不同的处境。

sentences.en: Esther wasn't some young white dude who was in it for a good time.
sentences.zh: 埃丝特不是那种为了找乐子而来的年轻白人小伙。

sentences.en: She was a 62-year-old immigrant entrepreneur who was constantly being criticized for the way she ran her business.
sentences.zh: 她是一位62岁的移民企业家，因为经营生意的方式而不断受到批评。

sentences.en: In an article from 1979, Esther said of Barry and Kim, quote,
sentences.zh: 在1979年的一篇文章中，埃丝特谈到巴里和金时说，引用：

sentences.en: They can go to hell.
sentences.zh: 让他们下地狱去吧。

sentences.en: They're the lowest of the low.
sentences.zh: 他们是人渣中的人渣。

sentences.en: I don't want them here.
sentences.zh: 我不希望他们在这里。

sentences.en: I don't care what they say.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎他们说什么。

sentences.en: They're liars.
sentences.zh: 他们是骗子。

sentences.en: I hate them.
sentences.zh: 我恨他们。

sentences.en: End quote.
sentences.zh: 引用结束。

sentences.en: If you just went off the context of that article, she sounded unhinged.
sentences.zh: 如果你只看那篇文章的语境，她听起来确实像疯了。

sentences.en: But this was a few months after the Trojan tape incident, and after hearing some of the things Barry put her through, I get why she seemed so angry.
sentences.zh: 但这发生在“特洛伊木马磁带”事件几个月后，在听了巴里对她做的一些事之后，我理解她为什么看起来那么愤怒。

sentences.en: This was her restaurant and her livelihood.
sentences.zh: 这是她的餐厅，也是她的生计。

sentences.en: Her frustration was justified, but in the press and in the wider music scene, she started to earn a very specific kind of reputation.
sentences.zh: 她的沮丧是有道理的，但在媒体和更广泛的音乐圈里，她开始获得一种非常特殊的声誉。

sentences.en: I think it was a stereotype, like Dragon Lady, they used to call her.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种刻板印象，他们过去常叫她“龙女”。

sentences.en: Jonathan Daniel, Madam Wong's booker again.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·丹尼尔，黄太太店的预订人再次发言。

sentences.en: People didn't realize how hard it was to be a woman, you know, let alone, like, not a white woman, doing that.
sentences.zh: 人们没有意识到作为一个女性有多难，你知道的，更不用说，还是一个非白人女性，做这件事有多难。

sentences.en: Like, it's insane that she did that and pulled it up.
sentences.zh: 她能做到并坚持下来简直不可思议。

sentences.en: But people didn't realize that.
sentences.zh: 但人们没有意识到这一点。

sentences.en: All the things that were her strengths became, like, the things that people would pick on as a stereotype.
sentences.zh: 她所有的优点都变成了人们用来攻击她的刻板印象。

sentences.en: Because she had the audacity to make her own business decisions and stand up for herself, Esther went from being called the godmother of punk to the dragon lady.
sentences.zh: 因为她有勇气做出自己的商业决策并为自己挺身而出，埃丝特从“朋克教母”变成了“龙女”。

sentences.en: I repeated that without really thinking about what it meant.
sentences.zh: 我重复了这个词，却没有真正思考它的含义。

sentences.en: Alice Bagg again.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝·巴格再次发言。

sentences.en: And now I realize that that is a racist term.
sentences.zh: 现在我意识到这是一个种族主义词汇。

sentences.en: So I want to apologize if, you know, I want to apologize for my ignorance and for using a term like that.
sentences.zh: 所以我想道歉，你知道，我想为我的无知和使用这样的词汇道歉。

sentences.en: I think it's easy to pick on people who you might see as, like, having less power than other people.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们很容易去攻击那些看起来比别人权力更小的人。

sentences.en: So if this was a club on the west side and it was run by an affluent white man, you might just think, oh, that's a business decision.
sentences.zh: 所以如果这是一家位于西区的俱乐部，由一位富有的白人男性经营，你可能只会觉得，哦，那是一个商业决策。

sentences.en: Punk music in Chinatown burned bright, but it burned faSt.
sentences.zh: 唐人街的朋克音乐燃烧得炽热，但也熄灭得很快。

sentences.en: Within a few years, the genre had evolved.
sentences.zh: 几年之内，这种流派就演变了。

sentences.en: And by 1981, bands like The Bags, The Alleycats, and The Dills, who helped define the sound of first wave L.A.
sentences.zh: 到了1981年，像The Bags、The Alleycats和The Dills这些帮助定义了第一波洛杉矶朋克之声的乐队，已经淡出了舞台。

sentences.en: punk, had drifted out of the scene.
sentences.zh: 朋克并没有消亡，但它在改变。

sentences.en: Punk wasn't dying, but it was changing.
sentences.zh: 这种音乐正被硬核乐队和观众所取代。

sentences.en: The music was being overtaken by hardcore bands and audiences.
sentences.zh: 它更快、更硬、更具侵略性，而且往往会带来非常不同的群体。

sentences.en: It was faster, harder, more aggressive, and tended to bring in a very different crowd.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想我们开始看到，比如光头党精神，还有白人男性运动员进入冲撞舞池，

sentences.en: Yeah, I think we started seeing, like, a skinhead ethos and also, like, a white male jocks getting into the slam pit
sentences.zh: 把事情搞得不再有趣，或者让那些曾经站在舞台前排的女性，

sentences.en: and kind of, like, taking it to a place where it wasn't fun or where the women that used to be at the front of the stage
sentences.zh: 突然感到不舒服，因为她们会，你知道，她们会受伤。

sentences.en: suddenly felt, like, uncomfortable being there because they would get, you know, they were going to get hurt.
sentences.zh: 香港咖啡馆的派对也结束了。

sentences.en: The party was over for the Hong Kong Cafe as well.
sentences.zh: 尽管很受欢迎，但他们在仅仅一年半后的1981年就关门大吉了。

sentences.en: Despite its popularity, they closed down shop in 1981 after just a year and a half.
sentences.zh: 其实根本没赚到什么钱。

sentences.en: There wasn't much money at all.
sentences.zh: 事情到了那个地步，金实际上对我说，他说，

sentences.en: And it just got to a point, Kim actually said to me, he said,
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，我想在新年后关门。

sentences.en: I'd like to close after New Year's if that's OK.
sentences.zh: 我说，我没意见。

sentences.en: And I said, it's OK with me.
sentences.zh: 埃丝特在黄太太店坚持得更久，派对又持续了几年。

sentences.en: Esther stuck it out with Madame Wong's Longer, and the party raged on for a few more years.
sentences.zh: 她的俱乐部成功熬过了朋克热潮和80年代初MTV的出现。

sentences.en: Her clubs managed to survive punk and the introduction of MTV in the early 1980s.
sentences.zh: 但过了一段时间，这些麻烦实在是不值得了。

sentences.en: But after a while, the hassle just wasn't worth it anymore.
sentences.zh: 埃丝特与她在唐人街的摇滚乐顾客之间建立的这种不可思议的联盟已经瓦解。

sentences.en: The improbable alliance that Esther formed with her rock-seeking customers in Chinatown had come apart.
sentences.zh: 1986年，她告诉《洛杉矶时报》，引用：

sentences.en: In 1986, she told the L.A.
sentences.zh: 现在来这里的孩子，他们快把我逼疯了。

sentences.en: Times, quote,
sentences.zh: 他们来到这里，表现得像被宠坏的顽童。

sentences.en: The kids that come here now, they drive me crazy.
sentences.zh: 有些人堵塞了我的厕所，还有一个人点燃了纸巾，触发了我们的喷淋系统，

sentences.en: They come here and they act like spoiled brats.
sentences.zh: 真是太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Some of them plugged up my toilets, and one man set fire to some paper towels and set off our sprinkler system,
sentences.zh: 我受够了。

sentences.en: flooding the whole basement.
sentences.zh: 把整个地下室都淹了。

sentences.en: It's got me pretty discouraged.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: After that fire in 1986, Esther announced that she was closing Madame Wong's East in Chinatown.
sentences.zh: 1986年那场火灾之后，埃丝特宣布她要关闭位于唐人街的“黄夫人东店”。

sentences.en: It's not clear if she regretted the experience, but when she was asked what she would miss most,
sentences.zh: 不清楚她是否对那段经历感到后悔，但当被问及她最怀念什么时，

sentences.en: she concluded, in her very straightforward way,
sentences.zh: 她以非常直率的方式总结道：

sentences.en: I'll miss the bands I liked, but I don't think I'll miss anything else.
sentences.zh: “我会怀念我喜欢的那些乐队，但我想我不会怀念其他任何东西。”

sentences.en: Not anymore.
sentences.zh: 再也不会了。

sentences.en: In 1991, after featuring bands like R.E.M., Guns N' Roses, and the Red Hot Chili Peppers,
sentences.zh: 1991年，在捧红了像R.E.M.、枪花乐队和红辣椒乐队之后，

sentences.en: Madame Wong's West closed its doors as well.
sentences.zh: “黄夫人西店”也关门大吉了。

sentences.en: By this time, Esther was well into her 70s, and the music landscape was a completely different place.
sentences.zh: 那时，埃丝特已经70多岁了，音乐界也已完全变了样。

sentences.en: Esther Wong died from emphysema in 2005 at the age of 88.
sentences.zh: 埃丝特·黄于2005年因肺气肿去世，享年88岁。

sentences.en: Even though her legacy was disputed over the years, the L.A.
sentences.zh: 尽管多年来她的遗产一直存在争议，《洛杉矶时报》

sentences.en: Times eulogized her as the godmother of punk.
sentences.zh: 还是称她为“朋克教母”。

sentences.en: You know, handed to them in Man and Wong's, you know, they thought of something new.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在黄夫人的店里，他们接触到了这些，他们想到了新东西。

sentences.en: They brought another crowd in.
sentences.zh: 他们带来了另一群人。

sentences.en: This is Ken Chan from Phoenix Bakery again.
sentences.zh: 这是凤凰饼家的陈先生。

sentences.en: Ken gets why the punk thing fascinated so many people, but he also kind of casually waves off this moment in the neighborhood's history.
sentences.zh: 陈先生理解为什么朋克文化会让那么多人着迷，但他对社区历史上的这一时刻表现得有些不以为然。

sentences.en: He's seen these fads come and go over the years.
sentences.zh: 多年来，他见惯了这些潮流来来去去。

sentences.en: I think the punk rock, you know, it was an era, it was a time, but it brought people into Chinatown.
sentences.zh: 我觉得朋克摇滚，你知道，那是一个时代，那是一段时光，但它确实把人们带到了唐人街。

sentences.en: You know, I think they maybe saw something on Chinese architectural.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想他们可能看到了中国建筑的一些东西。

sentences.en: Maybe they saw some knickknacks, but they got a little something in their memory bank.
sentences.zh: 也许他们看到了一些小玩意儿，但他们确实在记忆库里留下了一点东西。

sentences.en: Chinatown may have been, you know, deserted, may have been clothed, but, you know, we had a good time.
sentences.zh: 唐人街可能曾经，你知道，冷清过，可能曾经被遮蔽过，但，你知道，我们玩得很开心。

sentences.en: These two rock clubs meant so much to people in the punk scene.
sentences.zh: 这两个摇滚俱乐部对朋克圈的人来说意义重大。

sentences.en: But to someone like Ken, they're just a couple of stops on a walking tour of Central Plaza.
sentences.zh: 但对像陈先生这样的人来说，它们只是中央广场徒步游的几个站点而已。

sentences.en: These days, there are just too many bigger things to worry about.
sentences.zh: 如今，有太多更重要的事情需要担心了。

sentences.en: The neighborhood moved on, and after the punks left, the art galleries moved in.
sentences.zh: 社区在向前发展，朋克离开后，艺术画廊搬了进来。

sentences.en: And then the hipster restaurants.
sentences.zh: 然后是时髦的餐厅。

sentences.en: And then the developers.
sentences.zh: 接着是开发商。

sentences.en: Punk ended up just being a phase that, like so many people, Chinatown eventually grew out of.
sentences.zh: 朋克最终只是一个阶段，就像许多人一样，唐人街最终也从中成长并超越了它。
